plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding above value risks overpaying (winning at a price above value), while bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot second-price auction with no repeated interaction to exploit, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. My value is $28, so I will bid exactly that.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. This is because I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid, so bidding my true value maximizes my expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win with a bid above value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $47, I will bid $47 to ensure optimal outcomes.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49]. The optimal strategy in this setting is to bid truthfully shaded by (n-1)/n factor for uniform distributions, i.e., bid = value * (n-1)/n = 30 * 2/3 = 20. This balances winning probability against the price paid, maximizing expected profit given symmetric independent private values.
